Common AC Error Codes Indicating PCB Fault

Seeing a blinking light or an AC error code? It’s often a sign of a PCB fault. Here are some common examples we fix.

Error Code Common Meaning Potential Solution
E1/F1 Communication Error (Indoor/Outdoor) Check wiring, may require PCB repair or replacement.
E6 Motor or Fan Malfunction Could be the motor itself or the PCB’s control circuit.
CH05 / E5 Sensor Failure (Room/Coil) Test sensor; if okay, the fault lies in the PCB sensor circuit.
No Display Power Failure / Dead PCB Check main power. If power is present, the AC PCB needs repair.

Repair vs. Replace: Making the Right Choice

Unsure whether to repair or replace your faulty AC PCB? Here’s a breakdown to help you decide.

Pros of Repairing

  • Cost-Effective: Repairing is significantly cheaper than buying a new PCB, especially for inverter models. The AC circuit board repair cost is a fraction of the replacement price.
  • Eco-Friendly: Reduces electronic waste by extending the life of existing components.
  • Faster Solution: Often quicker than sourcing and waiting for a new, specific PCB model.
  • Maintains Originality: Keeps the original factory-fitted board in your AC unit.

Cons of Repairing

  • Not Always Possible: Severe damage (e.g., major burns, broken board) may be irreparable.
  • Finding Expertise: Requires a highly skilled AC PCB technician, which can be hard to find (but you’ve found us!).
  • Potential for Future Issues: If one component failed due to age, others might follow suit later on.
